finalJustifications: Because CloudFront with cache serves the statics of edge locations close to users — repeated requests do not even arrive at the origin, cutting transfer and load.
Because CloudFront transfers the traffic charge to the end user, who pays the delivery by the local access provider.
Because CloudFront compresses the fora EC2 of origin, reducing the cost of computing together with data transfer.
Because CloudFront requires migrating static files to the S3, whose transfer of exit to the internet is free.

optionReasons.saa-ini-199:option:0: Two separate ASGs duplicate management and do not coordinate base + peak — without combined policy balance between On-Demand and Spot it's manual..

optionReasons.saa-ini-199:option:3: 'Reserved' instances are not a type of launch of ASG — RI is collection discount, not group configuration.

finalJustifications: Because the mixed instance policy defines base On-Demand + extra capacity Spot and diversity between various types of instance in the MESMO group — lower cost and less impact of interruptions.
Because the mixed instances policy converts On-Demand instances into Spot without interruption, applying the discount without changing the group hardware.
Because mixed instances policy ensures that instances Spot of the group are never interrupted, protected by the contracted On-Demand base.
Because mixed instances policy requires at least three Auto Scaling Separate groups — one per purchasing model and one for diversification of types.

optionReasons.saa-ini-228:option:0: Alarms of the CloudWatch NOTIFICAM and trigger ad hoc actions — do not manage desired capacity or replace instances alone.
optionReasons.saa-ini-228:option:1: Spot is not self-substituted as a guarantee — the AWS closes when you need the capacity and the replacement depends on the availability/strategy configured.
optionReasons.saa-ini-228:option:2: The Beanstalk USA o Auto Scaling below — who effectively maintains the desired capacity and replenishes instances is EC2 Auto Scaling.

finalJustifications: Because EC2 Auto Scaling monitors health checks and replaces unhealthy instances by launching new Launch Template, keeping the desired capacity.
Because Auto Scaling restarts the loop-locked instance until it returns to the health checks configured.
Because Auto Scaling changes the application to the Lambda when the instance fails, keeping the service in the air without server.
Because Auto Scaling keeps a prepaid standby copy of each instance, promoted as soon as the original falls.

optionReasons.saa-ini-231:option:0: Round-robin DNS does not check health or react to real-time failures — customers cache IPs and continue beating in dead instance.
optionReasons.saa-ini-231:option:1: Sub-networks in several AZs do not distribute traffic by themselves — nothing routes requests automatically between instances.
optionReasons.saa-ini-231:option:2: The CloudFront It's CDN Cache on the edge — is not a load balancer between instances.

finalJustifications: Because ELB distributes requests among registered targets, monitors health via health checks and sends traffic only to healthy instances (ALB/NLB/GWLB).
Because ELB clones the instances EC2 recorded when traffic increases, absorbing overload with temporary replicas.
Because ELB store the responses in cache and serve the repeated requests alone, dispensing the instances of work.
Because ELB connects the user directly to the less busy instance via peer-to-peer, eliminating the intermediate of the route.

optionReasons.saa-ini-233:option:0: Dedicated Host is exclusive hardware DENTRO of an AZ — if the AZ falls, it falls together.
optionReasons.saa-ini-233:option:2: Different sub-networks in MESMA AZ share the same fate — AZ's failure knocks down all.
optionReasons.saa-ini-233:option:3: Restoring snapshots takes time and loses recent status — it is recovery, not continuous failure tolerance.

finalJustifications: Because instances in at least 2 AZs behind a ALB tolerate the loss of an entire AZ: the ALB detect and redirect 100% traffic to healthy AZ.
Because ALB Automatically rebuilds AZ instances that failed in another region, restoring the original capacity.
Because two AZs from the same region share the same physical datacenter, which makes the failover virtually instantaneous.
Because ALB duplicate each request for the two AZs simultaneously, and the fastest response is delivered to the user.

optionReasons.saa-ini-238:option:0: The central problem isn't DDoS — even without any attack, any hardware failure takes it all down.
optionReasons.saa-ini-238:option:2: A single instance usually costs MENOS, no more — there is no 'volume discount' that reverses this.
optionReasons.saa-ini-238:option:3: There is no fixed limit of 10.000 req/s imposed by AWS by instance.

finalJustifications: Because a single instance is a Single Point of Failure: any failure (hardware, OS, maintenance) will knock down the entire application — without redundancy there is no continuity.
Because a single instance in production violates the terms of use of the AWS, requiring minimum redundancy at two points of presence.
Because SPOF prevents the instance from receiving security updates: any patch would require the entire service to be dropped.
Because an instance alone cannot have fixed public IP, and each restart changes the address that users use to access the site.

optionReasons.saa-ini-255:option:1: Dedicated Hosts are Capacity FIXA and licensing face — the opposite of elasticity per second.
optionReasons.saa-ini-255:option:2: RI is COBRANCE discount for stable use — does not provide automatic scalability.
optionReasons.saa-ini-255:option:3: Spot can disappear in the middle of the peak just when you need it most — and it's not 'free''.

finalJustifications: Because On-Demand + Auto Scaling Group scale by metrics (CPU, Requisitions) and charge per second without commitment — the standard combination for unpredictable peaks.
Because On-Demand has priority of capacity over all other models, essential guarantee for unpredictable peaks.
Because ASG works only with On-Demand instances — Spot and Reserved cannot be automatically released by group.
Because the per second charge is exclusive to the instances managed by Auto Scaling — the manuals pay full time.

optionReasons.saa-ini-257:option:0: Group placement accelerates the network ENTRE instances in the same cluster — does not improve delivery to end users.
optionReasons.saa-ini-257:option:2: Even greater instance serves all of ONE point — more cost and without the proximity of the CDN.
optionReasons.saa-ini-257:option:3: The ALB DO NOT have built-in content cache — it only distributes requests.

finalJustifications: Because S3 + CloudFront is the pattern for statics: S3 scale the accommodation and the CloudFront delivery of edge locations Next — the EC2 Gets Free to Dynamics.
Because S3 executes the application code along with static files, unifying the entire site into a single service.
Because CloudFront converts the site into serverless automatically, transforming dynamic routes into edge functions.
Because S3 Static Website Hosting includes a built-in application server that processes content before delivery.
